findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises an exception
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start index (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset < 0`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing — `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). So whenever a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset while `enable_advanced_features` is on, the request will fail with a 500 error rather than returning a page. The comment claiming "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is incorrect.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime sort keys
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies Paginator.get_item_key, which does `int(math.floor(value) ...)` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `value` is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError. The paginator should have derived from DateTimePaginator (which converts datetimes to a millisecond integer key) or overridden get_item_key/value_from_cursor accordingly; as written, the optimized path will error as soon as build_cursor calls get_item_key on a result.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets, changing existing behavior for all endpoints
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` alters BasePaginator.get_result, which is shared by every cursor-paginated endpoint. Previously a non-prev cursor with a negative offset would surface an error from the ORM; now it is silently clamped to 0, so the client receives the first page again while believing it has paginated forward. This can produce infinite pagination loops (the returned next cursor recomputes from page 1) for any client that constructs a malformed negative offset. There is no explanation of why non-prev negative offsets must be clamped while prev negative offsets are passed through unchanged.

findings.title: Undocumented, permission-gated query parameter changes endpoint behavior with no API contract or tests
findings.body: A new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter switches the endpoint to a different paginator with different cursor semantics (negative offsets allowed, different key encoding) for superusers/global-access members. This is undocumented in the API surface (no serializer field, no publish-status note), and cursors produced by one paginator may not be interpretable by the other if a client toggles the parameter between requests, causing skipped/duplicated rows. No tests are added for the new paginator class, the negative-offset path, or the endpoint's gating logic.

findings.title: Comment-only change claims a capability the code does not implement
findings.body: The only change in cursors.py is a comment saying "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but the code (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged — Cursor already accepted any integer offset. The comment implies this PR enabled something in Cursor when it did not, which will mislead future maintainers about where the negative-offset behavior is actually implemented (and whether it is validated).
